title: Progressive availability ladders and adaptive rollback thresholds for model-variant rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood is expanding staged rollouts to support multiple model variants (full precision + quantized variants) and needs a deterministic, automated gating policy that protects latency SLOs and model quality during traffic shifts. Current rollouts are manual and lack explicit adaptive rollback thresholds tied to both service metrics and quality evals, which increases risk during peak traffic and when enabling aggressive quantized variants for cost savings.

Goal:
Define the SLO targets, error-budget triggers, and progressive rollout ladder for model-variant releases so that rollouts can be automated in Console with clear gates for: latency, availability, error rate, and quality regressions on a held-out prompt set. Provide specific numeric thresholds for canary, staged, and full rollouts and acceptance criteria for enabling quantized variants in Dedicated/Hosted modes.

Scope:
- SLOs for interactive (chat) and batch (embeddings) traffic for this release-control policy only.
- Rollout ladder: Canary (1%), Ramp (5%, 20%, 50%), Full (100%).
- Metrics considered: p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, 5xx error rate, per-prompt quality delta on a fixed eval prompt set, and error-budget burn rate.
- Implement Console gating rules and automatic rollback hooks; engineering to expose per-variant telemetry and evaluation signals.

Proposed SLO targets (baseline = currently deployed stable variant):
- Availability (regional): >= 99.95% (monthly)
- 95th percentile latency (chat first-token): <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 and absolute <= 400ms for hosted small region; for Dedicated target <= baseline_p95 * 1.10
- 99th percentile latency: <= baseline_p99 * 1.25 and absolute <= 900ms
- 5xx error rate: <= baseline_5xx + 0.1% absolute
- Quality on eval prompt set: relative degradation <= 1.0% (measured via semantic-similarity metric aggregated across prompts)
- Error budget: 0.05% monthly availability budget (burn tracked hourly)

Adaptive rollback & gating rules (automated):
1) Canary stage (1% traffic, 1 hour minimum):
   - Immediate rollback if p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.30 OR availability < 99.5% in the canary window OR 5xx increase > 0.5% absolute.
   - Hold if quality drop > 1.0% on eval set; require PM + ML lead approval to proceed.
   - Burn-rate check: if error budget burn rate > 10x against baseline within first hour, stop rollout and scale back.
2) Ramp stages (5% -> 20% -> 50%):
   - Each stage requires 2x stage-duration observation with no threshold breaches.
   - Stage duration configurable (default 60 minutes).
   - Thresholds tightened: p95 must remain <= baseline_p95 * 1.20; p99 <= baseline_p99 * 1.20; quality drop <= 0.8%.
   - If small transient breach (e.g., single spike) triggers but overall burn-rate < 3x, allow manual override with documented mitigation plan.
3) Full rollout (100%):
   - Only allowed when cumulative burn-rate <= 1.5x and monthly projected error budget usage remains < 25%.

Escalation and emergency rollback:
- SRE pager invoked if availability drops >0.5% absolute in any region for 15 continuous minutes during rollout.
- Automated rollback initiated if any of the following occur: p99 latency increase > 30% absolute, availability drop > 1.0% absolute, quality drop > 2.0% on eval set.

Implementation requirements for engineering:
- Per-variant telemetry exposing baseline comparison, aggregated quality delta from evaluation pipeline, and per-tenant SLO slices for first 24 hours of rollout.
- Console control plane support for defining the ladder and thresholds (UI + API).
- Release-control policy should be templated to allow per-tenant overrides (e.g., high-tier tenants with tighter SLOs).
- Integration test harness that simulates traffic shards and injects latency/error spikes to validate automated rollback behavior.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before this ticket is Done):
- PRD signoff by Product, SRE, and ML quality lead (names listed in comments).
- Console implements the policy UI and the API endpoint to create ladders with numeric thresholds.
- Telemetry PRs merged that provide per-variant p50/p95/p99, availability, 5xx %, and eval quality deltas with 1-minute resolution.
- End-to-end test that simulates the full ladder and demonstrates automated rollback triggers in staging (results uploaded to the release-control dashboard).
- Documentation: Runbook for rollout, decision matrix, and an example canary deployment for a quantized 4-bit variant.
- One successful pilot rollout to internal tenant group (3 tenants) with no automated rollback and burn-rate <= 1.0x across 48 hours.

Open questions & trade-offs:
- How to standardize 'quality metric' across different model types (chat vs. embeddings). Proposal: semantic-similarity + prompt-specific thresholds; ML team to own calibration.
- Default stage durations — conservative vs. faster ramp trade-off between cost and risk. Recommend configurable stages with safe defaults (60m).
- Per-tenant vs. global gating: allowing per-tenant overrides increases complexity but needed for enterprise SLAs.
